en: **First Chapter** **First Pāda** Now, therefore, [there follows] the desire to know Brahman. (1.1.1) The Section on the Desire to Know (Jijñāsā-adhikaraṇa). (1.1.1)
"That from which the origin and so forth of this [world proceed]. (1.1.2) The Section on Origin and So Forth (Janmādy-adhikaraṇa). (1.1.2)
Because [Brahman] has the scripture as its source. (1.1.3) The Section on Scripture Being the Source (Śāstrayonitva-adhikaraṇa). (1.1.3)
But that [Brahman is the cause] because of the harmony [of all scriptural texts]. 1.1.4. The Section on Harmony (Samanvaya-adhikaraṇa). 1.1.4.
"On account of seeing, [the cause] is not that which is not based on scripture. (1.1.5) The Section Concerning Seeing (Īkṣaty-adhikaraṇa). (1.1.5)
If it is argued that [the term "Self"] is used in a secondary sense, we say no, because of the word "Self. (1.1.6)
Because liberation is taught for one who is intent upon that [Brahman]. 1.1.7.
And because there is no statement of its being something to be abandoned. 1.1.8.
On account of [the Lord's] merging [into Himself]. 1.1.9.
Because of the commonality of their destination. 1.1.10.
And because it is so heard [in scripture]. 1.1.11.
The one consisting of bliss [is Brahman], because of the repetition. Sūtra 1.1.12. Section on the One Consisting of Bliss (Ānandamayādhikaraṇa). 1.1.12.
"If it be objected that [Brahman is not the cause] because of the word 'modification' (vikāra), we say no, because of abundance (prācurya). 1.1.13.
And because its cause is designated [in scripture]. 1.1.14.
And it is proclaimed as being based precisely on the wording of the mantra. 1.1.15.
Not the other, because it is not possible [otherwise]. 1.1.16.
And because there is a designation of difference. 1.1.17.
And because [the object] is directly perceived, there is no dependence on inference. 1.1.18.
And it teaches his union with That in this [state]. 1.1.19.
"On account of the teaching of its attributes within [the heart]. (1.1.20) The Section Concerning the Inner [Being] (Antar-adhikaraṇa). (1.1.20)
And [the Self] is other [than the body], because there is a designation of difference. 1.1.21.
"Ether [is Brahman], because of its characteristic marks. (1.1.22) This is the section concerning ether (ākāśādhikaraṇa). (1.1.22)
"Therefore, [it is] the vital breath (prāṇa). || 1.1.23 || Section on the Vital Breath (Prāṇādhikaraṇa) || 1.1.23 ||
"The light [is Brahman], because of the mention of its feet. (1.1.24) — The Section on the Light and the Feet (1.1.24).

"If it be argued that [the Self is not the object of meditation] because of the mention of 'desire' (chandas), we say no; for there is a declaration of the fixing of the mind [upon the Self], and such is seen [in other scriptural passages]. 1.1.25.
And because the designation of the quarters beginning with "the Beings" is thus appropriate. 1.1.26.
"If it be argued that [the Upanishads do not refer to Brahman] because of the difference in instruction, we say no; for there is no contradiction in either case. (1.1.27)
The vital breath [is Brahman], because it follows [the context]. 1.1.28. This is the section concerning Prātardana (1.1.28).
"If it be argued that [the Self taught here] is not the one to be known because the speaker teaches himself, we say no, for there is an abundance of internal connections in this [text]. (1.1.29)
But from the perspective of the scripture, there is instruction [of the Self as Brahman] just as in the case of Vāmadeva. (1.1.30)

"If it be objected that [the passage does not refer to Brahman] because of the marks of the individual soul (jīva) and the chief vital breath (mukhyaprāṇa), we say no; because of the threefoldness of meditation, and because that [threefoldness] is applicable here on account of [Brahman's] being the substratum. 1.1.31.
First Chapter. Second Quarter. Because of the teaching of what is well-known everywhere. (1.2.1) The Section Concerning What is Well-Known Everywhere (Sarvatraprasiddhyadhikaraṇa). (1.2.1)
And because the intended qualities are possible [in that case]. 1.2.2.
But because of the impossibility [of its being so], it is not the embodied soul. 1.2.3.
And because of the designation of [Brahman] as both the object and the agent of action. 1.2.4.
Because of the distinction in sound. 1.2.5.
And on account of Smṛti. 1.2.6.

"If it be argued that [Brahman] is not [the object of meditation] because of its having a small abode and because of the designation of it as such, we say no; for it is to be perceived as such, and it is like the ether. 1.2.7.
If it be argued that there is the attainment of enjoyment [in the intermediate state], we say no, because of the difference in nature. 1.2.8.
The Self [is meant], because of the inclusion of both the moving and the unmoving. (1.2.9) Section 1.2.9: The Topic of "Eating" (attradhikaraṇa).
And because of the context. 1.2.10.
"For the two selves have entered the cave, because of the vision thereof. (1.2.11) The Section Concerning Those Entered into the Cave (guhāpraviṣṭādhikaraṇa). (1.2.11)
And because of the qualification. 1.2.12.
Between the origination [of the body]. 1.2.13. The Section on the Intermediate State (Antarādhikaraṇa) 1.2.13.
And because of the designation of place and so forth. 1.2.14.
And [it is so] precisely because of the designation of that which is distinguished by bliss. 1.2.15.
And because there is a description of the path for one who has heard the Upaniṣads. 1.2.16.
"And because of non-abiding and impossibility, it is not the other. (1.2.17)
The Inner Ruler [is Brahman], because His attributes are designated in relation to the divine realm and so forth. (1.2.18) The Section Concerning the Inner Ruler (Antaryāmy-adhikaraṇa). (1.2.18)
Nor is it based on Smṛti, because its characteristics are not described as such. 1.2.19.
"And the embodied one; for both [schools] indeed study him as distinct [from the Self]. (1.2.20)
That which possesses the qualities of invisibility and so forth [is Brahman], because of the statement of its attributes. 1.2.21. The section concerning invisibility and so forth. 1.2.21.
"And because of the distinction and the designation of difference, it is neither of the other two. (1.2.22)
And because of the presentation of form. 1.2.23.
Vaiśvānara [is the Self], because of the qualification by a common term. 1.2.24.
"That which is being remembered would be an inference. (1.2.25)

If it be argued that [the Self] is not [the object of knowledge] because of its being mentioned along with sound and so forth, and because of its being established within, we say no; for there is instruction regarding such a vision, because [otherwise] it would be impossible, and they also study this as the Puruṣa. 1.2.26.
For this very reason, [the Self] is neither a deity nor an elemental being. 1.2.27.
Jaimini [maintains] that there is no contradiction even with direct perception. 1.2.28.
"Because of manifestation," says Āśmarathya. (1.2.29)
Bādari [maintains that the soul's departure] is for the sake of remembrance. 1.2.30.
And they enjoin this [breath] in this [context]. 1.2.32.
**First Chapter** **Third Section** **Sūtra 1.3.1:** "The abode of heaven, earth, and so forth [is Brahman], because of its own word. **Topic 1.3.1:** The Abode of Heaven, Earth, and So Forth.
Because there is the designation of that which is to be approached by the liberated. 1.3.2.
It is not inference, because of the word "that" (atad). 1.3.3.
And [the word "prāṇin" (living being) is used] for one who possesses breath. 1.3.4.
On account of the designation of difference. 1.3.5.
On account of the context. 1.3.6.
And on account of abiding and eating. (1.3.7)
The Infinite [is Brahman], because it is taught as being superior to the serene faith (samprasāda). 1.3.8. Section on the Infinite (bhūmādhikaraṇa). 1.3.8.
And because of the logical consistency of the doctrine. 1.3.9.
The Imperishable [is Brahman], because it supports that which has the sky as its limit. (1.3.10) The Section on the Imperishable (Akṣarādhikaraṇa). (1.3.10)
And that [is so] because of the command. 1.3.11.
And because of the exclusion of other states. 1.3.12.
"He is [Brahman], because of the designation of Him as the object of the act of seeing. (1.3.13) The Section on the Object of the Act of Seeing. (1.3.13)
The small [ether] [is Brahman], because of the subsequent [passages]. 1.3.14. The Section on the Small [Ether] (Daharādhikaraṇa). 1.3.14.
For it is seen from both movement and sound, as well as from the inferential mark. 1.3.15.
And because this greatness of steadfastness is perceived in him. 1.3.16.
And because of common renown. 1.3.17.
"If it be argued that he [is the one referred to] because of the reference to the other, we say no, because of impossibility. (1.3.18)
If it be argued that [the soul's true nature] manifests from the north [heaven], we reply: "But [its] true nature has indeed already manifested. (1.3.19)
And the reference has another purpose. 1.3.20.
If it be argued that [the individual soul] has little learning, that has already been answered. 1.3.21.
And because of the imitation of that [sun]. Sūtra 1.3.22. Section on Imitation (Anukṛti-adhikaraṇa). 1.3.22.
Moreover, it is recorded in traditional scripture (Smṛti). 1.3.23. 1.3.23.
He is known from the word alone. 1.3.24. The section concerning that which is known [from scripture]. 1.3.24.
But with respect to the heart, [the Sūtra says] "because human beings are the qualified [subjects]," 1.3.25.
Bādarāyaṇa [maintains that] even beyond that [the path of the fathers], there is [attainment of Brahman], because it is possible; this is the section concerning the deities (Devatādhikaraṇa). 1.3.26.
If it be argued that there is a contradiction regarding action, we say no, because we observe multiple ways of attaining [the goal]. 1.3.27.
If it be argued that [the world] is sound, we say no, because it originates from this [Brahman], as is known through perception and inference. 1.3.28.
And for this very reason, there is eternality. 1.3.29.
"And because name and form are the same, there is no contradiction even in the case of repetition, on account of both scripture and tradition. (1.3.30)
Jaimini [holds that] there is no entitlement [to the knowledge of Brahman] for those such as the Madhukaras, because [the requirements for it] are impossible in their case. 1.3.31.
And because of the mention of luminaries [in the context of the states of existence]. 1.3.32.
But Bādarāyaṇa [holds that there is] existence, for it indeed exists. (1.3.33)
For it is indicated by the hearing of Śuka’s disregard [for the Vedas] and his subsequent rushing toward them. (1.3.34) The Section Concerning Non-Śūdras (Apaśūdrādhikaraṇa). (1.3.34)
And because of the attainment of the status of a Kṣatriya later on, as indicated by the sign of Caitraratha. (1.3.35)
Because of the misapprehension of mental formations and because of the expression of the non-existence of that [self]. (1.3.36)
And because [the scripture] proceeds toward the determination of the non-existence of that [self]. (1.3.37)
On account of the prohibition of hearing, studying, and understanding the meaning [of the Veda], and because of Smṛti. 1.3.38.
On account of trembling. Section 1.3.39: The Section on Trembling.
On account of the vision of light. Section 1.3.40: The Topic of Light (Jyotir-adhikaraṇa).

Space [is distinct from the Self], because of its designation as being a different entity and so forth. (Sūtra 1.3.41) The Section Concerning the Designation of Being a Different Entity and So Forth (Arthāntaratvādivyapadeśādhikaraṇa). (1.3.41)
"On account of the difference between deep sleep and departure [from the body]. Section 1.3.42: The Topic on Deep Sleep.
[The suffix *taddhita* is applied] after words such as *pati* and others. 1.3.43.

**First Chapter** **Fourth Pāda** **Sūtra 1.4.1:** "If it be argued that [the Self] is inferential according to some, we say no, because of the apprehension [of the Self] as presented in the allegory of the body; and the scripture also shows this. **Topic: The Section on the Inferential (Ānumānikādhikaraṇa)**
But that [body] is subtle because it is fit for that [state]. 1.4.2.
Because it is dependent on that [Brahman], [the world] is purposeful. 1.4.3.
And because [the Lord] is not mentioned as being an object of knowledge. 1.4.4.
If it be argued that [the Self] speaks, we say no; for the wise one [is meant], according to the context. 1.4.5.
And thus, there is both the presentation and the question regarding these three alone. 1.4.6.
And like the Great [Self]. 1.4.7.
Like the cup, because there is no distinction; this is the section concerning the cups (Camasādhikaraṇa). 1.4.8.
But [the soul] has light as its starting point, for thus it is studied by some. 1.4.9.
"And because there is instruction regarding mental construction, as in the case of honey and so forth, there is no contradiction. (1.4.10)

[The Sāṅkhya doctrine is] not [to be accepted], even because of the inclusion of a number, on account of the plurality [of the principles] and because of the excess [over that number]. 1.4.11. The Section Concerning the Inclusion of a Number (1.4.11).
The vital breaths and so forth [are the five fires], because of the supplementary statement. 1.4.12.
According to some, there is light [as food] when food is absent. 1.4.13.

And because of the statement regarding ether and the rest as being causes, exactly as they have been described. (Sūtra 1.4.14) — This is the section concerning causality (Kāraṇatvādhikaraṇa). (1.4.14)
Because of attraction. 1.4.15.
On account of [the word *jagat*] denoting the world; [this is] the section concerning Bālāki (1.4.16).

If it be argued that [the Brahman] is not [meant here] because of the characteristic marks of the individual soul (jīva) and the chief vital breath (mukhyaprāṇa), that has already been explained. 1.4.17.
But Jaimini [holds that the passage] has another meaning, on account of both the question and the explanation; and thus also some [teachers]. 1.4.18.
On account of the syntactical connection [of the words with the whole sentence]. Sūtra 1.4.19. Section on the Syntactical Connection of the Sentence (Vākyānvayādhikaraṇa). 1.4.19.
Āśmarathya [holds that] there is a mark for the establishment of the proposition. 1.4.20.
Auḍulomi [maintains that the soul departs] from such a state as it is about to transmigrate. 1.4.21.
"On account of the abiding [of the world in Brahman], so says Kāśakṛtsna. (1.4.22)
And [Brahman] is the material cause, because there is no contradiction with the initial proposition and the illustrative examples. (1.4.23) The Section on Material Cause (Prakṛtyadhikaraṇa). (1.4.23)
And because of the teaching of covetousness. 1.4.24.
"And because both [the individual soul and Brahman] are directly mentioned [in the text]. (1.4.25)
Because of self-origination and transformation. 1.4.26.
For it is indeed proclaimed as the womb. 1.4.27.
By this, all [objections] have been explained, have been explained. 1.4.28. This concludes the section on the explanation of all [objections]. 1.4.28.

**Second Chapter** **First Pāda** **Sūtra 2.1.1:** If it be argued that there would be the fault of leaving no room for the Smṛtis, we say no, because that would entail the fault of leaving no room for other Smṛtis. **Topic: The Authority of the Smṛtis (Smṛtyadhikaraṇa)**
And because the others are not perceived. (2.1.2)
By this, Yoga is refuted. (2.1.3) The Section on the Refutation of Yoga. (2.1.3)

Not so, because this [world] has different characteristics; and its being such [as described by scripture] is due to the Word [of Scripture]. (2.1.4) The Section on "Because of Not Having Different Characteristics" (2.1.4).
"But there is a designation of the presiding deity, on account of distinction and on account of following after. (2.1.5)
But it is indeed seen. 2.1.6.
If it is argued that [the world] is non-existent, we say no, because [that statement] is a mere negation. 2.1.7.
[The doctrine is] untenable because, upon dissolution, the same undesirable consequence would follow. (2.1.8)
But it is not so because of the existence of examples. 2.1.9.
And because of the defects in one's own position. 2.1.10.
"Even because reasoning is not firmly established, if it is argued that the object of inference must be otherwise, even so there follows the consequence of no liberation. (2.1.11)
By this, those [theories] not accepted by the learned are also explained. (2.1.12) The Section on Those Not Accepted by the Learned (Śiṣṭāparigrahādhikaraṇa). (2.1.12)

If it be argued that there is no distinction [between the two] because of the attainment of the state of being an enjoyer, [we reply: it may be so, as in the case of the world. (2.1.13) The Section on the Attainment of the State of Being an Enjoyer (Bhoktrāpatty-adhikaraṇa). (2.1.13)
The non-difference of that [effect] from that [cause] follows from such terms as "originating" (ārambhaṇa) and others. (2.1.14) — The Section on Originating (Ārambhaṇādhikaraṇa). (2.1.14)
And because [the self] is perceived when there is existence. 2.1.15.
And because of the existence of what follows. 2.1.16.

"If it be argued that [the soul] does not [exist] because of the designation of its non-existence, we say no; for there is another attribute [intended], according to the remainder of the sentence. (2.1.17)
On account of reasoning and another scriptural passage. 2.1.18.
And like a cloth. 2.1.19.
And as in the case of the vital breath and so forth. 2.1.20. 2.1.20.

The objection that the defects of not performing what is beneficial and so forth would follow [for Brahman] because of its being designated as something else. (Sūtra 2.1.21) Section on Designation as Something Else (2.1.21).
But it is more [than one], because of the designation of distinctions. 2.1.22.
And like a stone and so forth, that [creation] is impossible. 2.1.23.

"If it be said that [the Lord] is not [the material cause] because we observe the withdrawal [of the world at dissolution], we say no, for it is like milk. (2.1.24) The section concerning the observation of withdrawal (upasaṃhāradarśana). (2.1.24)
And [the soul's size] is like that of the gods and others in the world. 2.1.25.

"Either the entire [Brahman] would be affected, or there would be a contradiction with the scriptural texts concerning its partlessness. (2.1.26) The Section on the Consequence of the Affection of the Whole (Kṛtsnaprasaktyadhikaraṇa). (2.1.26)
But on account of scripture, because it has its root in the Word [of Śruti]. 2.1.27.
For [the world] is both within the Self and manifold. 2.1.28.
And because of the defects in their own position. 2.1.29.
"And [the Lord] is endowed with all [powers], because of the vision of Him. This is the section concerning [the Lord] being endowed with all [powers]. (2.1.30)
"If it be argued that [the Lord] does not [act] because He is devoid of instruments, that has already been answered. (2.1.31)
[The world] is not [unreal], because it possesses a purpose. (Sūtra 2.1.32) The Section on Possessing a Purpose (Prayojanavattvādhikaraṇa) 2.1.32.
But as in the world, [the Lord's activity] is mere sport (līlā). 2.1.33.
There is no partiality or cruelty [on the part of the Lord], because He has regard for [the karma of beings]; for thus Scripture shows. (2.1.34) The Section on Partiality and Cruelty (2.1.34).
"If it be argued that [the distinction between the two states] does not exist because there is no differentiation of karma, we say no, because [the cycle] is beginningless. (2.1.35)
And it is both logically established and empirically perceived. (2.1.36)
And because all dharmas are possible. [Sūtra 2.1.37] This is the section concerning the possibility of all dharmas. [Adhikaraṇa 2.1.37]

**Second Chapter** **Second Pāda** **Sūtra 2.2.1:** And because the arrangement [of the world] is impossible, there is no inference [of a creator]. The Section on the Impossibility of the Arrangement [of the World] (Racanānupapattyadhikaraṇa) 2.2.1.
And because of the activity [of the world]. 2.2.2.
If it is argued that [the soul] is like water in a vessel, [we reply] that this is also the case there. 2.2.3.
And because there is no stability in their distinction, as they are independent. 2.2.4.
And because it does not exist elsewhere, like grass and such things. (2.2.5)
Even if it were admitted [that the self exists], there would still be an absence of purpose. 2.2.6.
If it is argued that it is like a man and a stone, even so [the objection remains]. (2.2.7)
And because the status of being the principal [of a compound] is untenable. 2.2.8.
And because, otherwise, there would be an absence of the capacity for cognition in inference. (2.2.9)
And because of contradictions, [the Sāṃkhya system] is untenable. 2.2.10.
Or [the production of] the large and the long is like [the production of] the short and the circular. 2.2.11. Section on the Large and the Long. 2.2.11.
In either case, there is no action; therefore, that [creation] is non-existent. (2.2.12) The section concerning the fact that atoms are not the cause of the world. (2.2.12)
And because of the admission of inherence, there would be an infinite regress due to its being on the same footing [as the categories it relates]. (2.2.13)
And because it exists eternally. 2.2.14.
And because it possesses form and other qualities, the opposite [of the soul's nature] follows from observation. (2.2.15)
And because there would be faults in either case. (2.2.16)
And because of non-possessiveness, there is absolute lack of concern. 2.2.17.
Even if both [the self and the aggregates] were the cause, that [self] would not be attained. 2.2.18. Section on the Aggregate (Samudāyādhikaraṇa). 2.2.18.
If it be argued that [the world] exists because of mutual dependence, we say no, because [the elements] are merely the causes for the origination [of one another]. (2.2.19)
And because the preceding ceases when the succeeding arises. (2.2.20)
If it did not exist, there would be a contradiction of the proposition; otherwise, there would be simultaneity. (2.2.21)
The non-attainment of analytical and non-analytical cessation [is established] because there is no interruption. 2.2.22.
And because there would be faults in either case. 2.2.23.
And [the same applies] to space, because there is no distinction. 2.2.24.
And because of the absence of memory [of such a body]. 2.2.25.
Not from the non-existent, because that has not been observed. 2.2.26.
And in this same way, there is the accomplishment of even those who dwell in the north. 2.2.27.
"Not non-existence, because of perception" (2.2.28). This is the section on non-existence (nābhāvādhikaraṇa) 2.2.28.
And because of the difference in nature, [the world] is not like a dream and so forth. (2.2.29)
There is no existence, because it is not perceived. 2.2.30.
And because of momentariness. 2.2.31.
And because it is impossible in every way. (2.2.32)
"Not in one [body], because of impossibility" (2.2.33). This is the section concerning the impossibility in one [body] (ekasmin-asambhava-adhikaraṇa) (2.2.33).
And thus, there would be a partiality of the self. 2.2.34.
And there is no non-contradiction even through figurative interpretation, because of transformation and other reasons. (2.2.35)
And because of the persistence of the final state, and because both are eternal, there is no distinction. 2.2.36.
On account of the inconsistency of the Lord [being the cause], [the doctrine of Pradhāna is not tenable]. Sūtra 2.2.37. Section on the Lord (Paty-adhikaraṇa) 2.2.37.
And because a relationship [between them] is untenable. 2.2.38.
And because the existence of a substratum is untenable. 2.2.39.
If it be argued that [the soul] is like an instrument, we say no, because of enjoyment and so forth. 2.2.40.
Either it would have an end, or it would lack omniscience. 2.2.41.
On account of the impossibility of origination. || 2.2.42 || The Section on the Impossibility of Origination. || 2.2.42 ||
And the instrument does not belong to the agent. 2.2.43.
Or, if consciousness and the rest do exist, there is no refutation of that [self]. 2.2.44.
And because of contradiction. 2.2.45.
**Second Chapter** **Third Section** **Sūtra 2.3.1:** *Not [so] ether, because it is not mentioned [in the scripture].* The Topic of Ether (Viyan-adhikaraṇa).
But it does exist. 2.3.2. 2.3.2.
Because of the impossibility of [the word] *goṇī* [denoting the cow]. 2.3.3.
And from scripture. 2.3.4.
And it may belong to one [thing], as in the case of the word "Brahman. (2.3.5)
There is no abandonment of the thesis because there is no distinction from words. 2.3.6.
But as far as there is modification, there is division, as in the case of the world. (2.3.7)
By this, Mātariśvan is explained. (Sūtra 2.3.8) The Section on Mātariśvan (2.3.8).
But [the origination] of that which exists is impossible, because it is not logically tenable. (2.3.9) The Section on Impossibility (Asambhavādhikaraṇa). (2.3.9)
Fire [proceeds] from that, for thus the scripture says. (2.3.10) The Section on Fire (Tejo'dhikaraṇa). (2.3.10)
Water. 2.3.11. Topic: The non-obstruction [of water]. 2.3.11.
On account of the context of earth, and because of the word "form" and others [at the end of the passage]. (2.3.12) The section concerning the context of earth. (2.3.12)
"But he [attains that] from the meditation on that alone, because of its characteristic mark. (2.3.13) This is the section concerning meditation on that. (2.3.13)
